definitions.definition: Floor plate that is part of the midbrain.

Portion of tissue that gives rise to the lens. The lens of the zebrafish forms by delamination of lens placodal cells and not through invagination. This results in a solid spherical mass as opposed to a hollow lens vesicle. Detachment of the solid lens vesicle of zebrafish at 24-26 hpf is accomplished in part by apoptosis, similar to mammals.

properties.value: Dbxref for ZFIN changed to match actual database accession number.  Old Dbxref ZDB-ANAT-090226-2 correct Dbxref ZDB-ANAT-090227-6.

definitions.definition: Multi-tissue comprised of neurons, dendrites, axon terminals, glial cells, and capillaries.

name: medial motor nucleus of vagal nerve

synonyms.name: medial motor nucleus of vagal nerve

definitions.definition: Motor nucleus of vagal nerve that is located within the medial portion of rhombomere 8.

Hindbrain nucleus which consists of cell bodies whose axons exit the hindbrain via cranial nerve VIII and innervate hair cells of the lateral line and inner ear. The neurons of these nuclei are unusual in that they extend both contra- and ipsilateral dendrites.
Multi-tissue structure that is the external layer of the swim bladder that is covered by the peritoneum, and made of elastic fibres and ichthyocol (short needles of collagen).

Multi-tissue structure that is the internal layer of the swim bladder and is comprised of thin endoderm and a smooth muscle layer called the muscularis mucosa with longitudinal and circular fibres with some collagen.

A portion of tissue that gives rise to the scale.  At the  initial stages the primordium  is composed of an accumulation of fibroblast below the basil epidermis.   As the primordium develops the epidermis over the fibroblast alters: the basal epidermal cells become cuboidal and narrow, the collagen matrix remodels and the hemidesmosomes disappear.
Portion of tissue that is part of the valvula cerebelli and contains Purkinje cells.
Portion of tissue that consists of axons of cerebellar granule cells that synapse onto Purkinje cell dendrites.
Otic vesicle protrusion that is initially ventrally located and then fuses with the lateral protrusion, giving rise to the pillar of the lateral semicircular canal.

inverseRoles.relatedName: pillar of the lateral semicircular canal

definitions.definition: Multi-tissue structure that is part of the heart tube and will become the cardiac ventricle.

roles.relatedName: presumptive cardiac ventricle primitive heart tube

definitions.definition: Multi-tissue structure that is part of the primitive heart tube and will become the cardiac atrium.
Portion of tissue that is part of the heart tube and will become the atrioventricular canal.
Artery that is part of the pharyngeal arches.
Aortic arch that is part of pharyngeal arch 1. The paired aortic arch 1 arteries branch off of the ventral aorta, and empty into the right and left lateral dorsal aorta.

The mesencephalic veins (MsV) enter the mid cerebral veins (MCeV) at the dorsal midline. THe MCeVs originate at the dorsal midline, proceed laterally in a ventral direction to drain into the paired primordial midbrain channels (PHBC).

Aortic arch that is part of pharyngeal arch 6. Aortic arch 6 artery is paired and has a common trunk with aortic arch 5 from the ventral aorta, and drains via a separate branch of the lateral dorsal aorta. Aortic arches 5 and 6 supply the trunk and tail with oxygenated blood.
Artery that exits the gill filament.
Arterioles which take blood from the gill lamella to the efferent  filamental arteries.
Extend upward from the PCS, branch to provide an arterial feed to the hindbrain, then drain back down into the PHBC.
Is an interconnected tubular multi-tissue structure that contains fluid that is actively transported around trunk.

Vein that branches off the nasal ciliary artery.  Initially, at 2dpf, the dorsal ciliary vein (DCV) drains into the primordial midbrain channel (PMBC) or the PMBC/PHBC junction.  Later, by 3.5dpf,  the DCV drains into the optic choroid vascular plexus.  The dorsal branch of the inner optic circle drains into the DCV.
Vessel that connects to the primitive hindbrain channel and the basilar artery at the caudal end of the medulla oblongata.

Vein that drains the vascular plexus of the midgut and hindgut.  At early stages the subintestinal vein (SIV) drains into the PCV and the CCV.  At later stages the SIV drains into the hepatic sinusoid.  The SIV are begin as paired veins.   After 4dpf the remains of the left SIV forms separate segments that empty into the right SIV and eventually merge with the right.  At 3dpf the rostral end of  left SIV begins to form the reticular hepatic sinusoids.  The portion of the left SIV caudal to the hepatic sinusoid forms the hepatic portal vein.
Arteries that irrigate rostral regions of the midbrain. They extend between the basal communicating artery to the anterior cerebral vein.
Vein that drains the median palatocerebral vein into the optic vein.
Muscular layer of the cardiac ventricle composed of a compact myocardial layer surrounding the trabecular layer.
The outer layer the ventricular myocardium, muscle  fibers are arranged in a compact form and involved the entire ventricle.
Anatomical system located in the heart that initiates and propagates heart contraction.  The cardiac pacemaker.
The atrioventricular valve has four distinct leaflets oriented anterior, posterior, left, and right of the atrioventricular orifice.
The portion of tissue in the atrioventricular canal that slows impulse propagation between the atrium and cardiac ventricle.
An elaborate set of vessels that branch off caudally from the anterior mesenteric artery just after the dorsal aorta.  The SBA vascular loops are located on the ventral side of the swim bladder.
Vein that  is fed by the nasal artery.  It  rises dorsally around the front of the head, draining into the ACeV and eventually into the PMBC on either side.
Is an interconnected tubular multi-tissue structure that contains fluid that is actively transported around the caudal fin.
Artery that is positioned in the intraray mesenchyme between the hemirays of the lepidotrichia.
Vein that flanks and is just lateral to the fin ray, in the interray mesenchyme.
Stripe of tissue on the dorsal side of the fish, fated to become the dorsal region of the median fin fold.

A network of blunt ended vessels lacking direct connection to the blood vascular system.  These vessels collect and drain fluids and macromolecules from interstitial spaces throughout the animal.  They derive from a subpopulation of endothelial cells and have walls that are much thinner than the blood carrying vessels.  The walls are mostly composed of single layer of irregularly shaped endothelial cells.  Lymphatic vessels are usually classified as either superficial or deep.
The thoracic duct is the first perfused lymphatic, located between the dorsal aorta and posterior cardinal vein.

One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.)
Dorsal region of the axial hypoblast.
Outer layer of the dental organ.

A structure that is involved in tooth formation.  A bell shape two layer  epithelial structure that descends toward the ceratobranchial 5 bone, enclosing the dental mesenchyme.  At later times in tooth development the cells at the apex of the bell may be involved in enameloid formation.  This structure remains at the base of the erupted tooth and is the source of replacement teeth.
Tissue of the developing tooth. It is composed of pre-odontoblast and undifferentiated mesenchyme cells and connects to the basal lamina.
Iridescent iridophore containing gold reflecting platelets.
Tela chorioidea that lines the tectal ventricle.
Ducts that transport enzymes between organs in the digestive system.
Intercellular space surrounded by the basal surface of the hepatocytes that collect bile.

properties.value: Should be located in rather then part_of when we get the appropriate relation.

definitions.definition: Vein that is central to a lobule in the liver.
Portion of the liver which develops on the fish's right side adjacent to the gall bladder.

A primary motor neuron of the spinal cord. This cell is present in slightly less than half of the trunk hemisegments. Additionally, this cell has at least 2 different fates: it may become a primary motoneuron and arborize in an exclusive muscle territory, or it may die during embryonic development.

properties.value: This term is a leaf node in the zebrafish AO and is not in the CL.

definitions.definition: Hindbrain interneuron that is part of rhombomere 1 with twelve neurons in each hemi-rhombomere. Axon runs in the dorsal spinal cord. The RoL1 stem axon projects ipsilaterally along the brain stem and spinal cord. From the more lateral location of its spinal axon, RoL1's collaterals projected both ventrally and medially.  The branching of RoL1 collaterals within the medulla, occur at multiple levels.

properties.value:
May have 12  neurons in each hemi rhombomere ZDB-PUB-060217-9.
7 neurons in each hemi rhombomere 080227-17 and 931014-770.

definitions.definition: Hindbrain interneuron, part of rhombomere 6, with one caudal-medial neuron in each hemi-rhombomere.  The fibers pass through the medial longitudinal fasciculus.

properties.value: This term is a leaf node in the zebrafish AO and is not in the CL.

definitions.definition: A RoL2 interneuron that is part of rhombomere 2.
Hindbrain interneuron that is part of rhombomere 32 with two medial neurons in each hemi-rhombomere.
CNS interneurons located in the midbrain.
Midbrain interneuron at the caudal position in the lateral midbrain.

A larval melanophore stripe that forms a band, of pigmentation extending from the bases of the eyes on each side of the midline to the top of the tail, that underlies the myotomes bilaterally, still is dorsal to the yolk.
Lip that covers the lower portion of the mouth.
Kolmer-Agduhr neurons are ciliated GABAergic neurons that contact the central canal of the spinal cord and have ipsilateral ascending axons.
A ciliated epithelial cell with many cilia.

Interneurons of the spinal cord that arise from the V1 proliferation domain.  The CiA neurons inhibit motoneurons, other ventral interneurons and also inhibit dorsal sensory neurons involved in sensory gating,.  CiA have ipsilateral axonal projections in both motor and sensory regions of spinal cord.
Is an interconnected tubular multi-tissue structure that contains fluid that is actively transported around the organism.
Microvessel of the blood circulation system lined with vascular endothelial cells.
Caudal procurrent ray that is ventrally located on the caudal fin skeleton.  There are 5 ventral procurrent rays in the caudal fin.
A muscle that brings a body part closer to the sagittal plane of the body.

Immature reproductive tissue that has not undergone final maturation into either testis or ovary. During gonadal development, the gonad may be  transiently intersexual where there is a  parallel presence of both oocytes and spermatocytes.
Muscle, composed of long cylindrical, multinucleated cells that attaches to the skeleton via tendons.
Capillary that is part of the renal glomerulus. Glomerular capillary endothelial membranes in zebrafish normally have a fenestrated morphology that is visible at the ultrastructural level.
Layer of the glomerular basement membrane adjacent to the glomerular capillary.
Renal tubule that connects to the renal corpuscle.
Blood vessel part of cranial vasculature.
Lymph vessel part of fin.
Blood vessel part of pectoral fin.

Membrane between the pronephric podocytes and the pronephric glomerular capillaries.  It is a trilaminar structure composed of the fused basement membranes of the glomerular capillaries and basement membrane of the podocytes.  The capillary membranes touch the GBM at contact points that are separated by pores.  The membrane is semi-permeable allowing water and small molecules to pass into the renal capsular space.
Any of the tubular multi-tissue structures through which blood circulates in the body.

The functional webs of the paired fins.  They arise as a consequence of apical fold (AER) expansion and of migration of the distal mesenchyme. The fin folds are delimited by a dorsal and a ventral striated epidermis. The cells of the epidermal basal stratum are positioned on a basement membrane. Directly beneath the basement membrane of each side there is an array of actinotrichs, fibers of the extracellular matrix which act as supportive elements of the larval fin folds.
Ionocyte located in the gills.
Integument ionocyte rich in Na,K-ATPase.
A non-terminally differentiated cell that originates from the neural crest and differentiates into an iridophore.
A non-terminally differentiated cell that originates from the neural crest and differentiates into a cyanophore.
Posterior protrusion of the third ventricle.
Portion of the pancreatic duct, external to the pancreas body that connects the pancreas with the hepatopancreatic ampulla.
Dorsal fin pterygiophore that is caudal to  pterygiophore 1 of the dorsal fin.
Dorsal fin pterygiophore that is caudal to  pterygiophore 7 of the dorsal fin. The most caudal pterygiophore of the dorsal fin.
First distal radial of the dorsal fin.
Fifth distal radial of the dorsal fin.
Sixth proximal radial of the dorsal fin.

Sensory canal between and in close proximity posteriorly with the post-otic and preoperculo-mandibular sensory canals, and anteriorly with the supraorbital and infraorbital sensory canals. The otic sensory canal is bilaterally paired.

Sensory canal contained in the nasal and frontal bones.  It contains 4 or 5 neuromast. The first neuromast is positioned in the tubular nasal bone and the other neuromasts are located in the frontal bone.  The canal is anterior to and in close proximity to the otic and infraorbital sensory canals. The supraorbital sensory canal is bilaterally paired.
Actinotrichium that is part of the anal fin skeleton.
Barbel that is associated with the anterior nostril. Anterior nasal barbel is paired.
The dorsal part of the ear. Comprises the three semicircular canals, which connect to the utricle.
Foramen in the inner ear.
Joint that articulates autopalatine and vomer bones. Autopalatine vomer joint is paired.
Foramen in the bone or cartilage comprising the anterior wall of the orbit, and through which passes at least the deep ophthalmic branch of cranial nerve V (trigeminal).
Barbel that originates on the chin.
Sensory nerve that innervates the pectoral fin.
Pectoral fin motor nerve that enters the fin from the dorsal side of the fin caudal of nerve 1 and rostral of all other motor nerves and innervates the dorsal side of the pectoral fin.
Joint that articulates the ceratohyal and dorsal hypohyal bones. Ceratohyal-dorsal hypohyal joint is paired.
Joint that articulates the left and right hypobranchial 3 cartilages or bones. Inter-hypobranchial 3 joint is unpaired.
Joint that articulates the pterosphenoid and orbitosphenoid. Pterosphenoid-orbitosphenoid joint is paired.
Fossa where the hyomandibula articulates with the sphenotic and prootic to form the hyomandibular-otic region joint.
Is a bony partially gas filled sphere located ventral and anterior to the inner ear.  The prootic bulla is paired.
Joint between the centra, and sometimes the neural arches or parapophyses of vertebra 4 and vertebra 5.

Mental barbel that originates on the chin, in an anteromedial position relative to the outer mental barbel. The inner mental barbel is nearer to the mandibular symphysis than is the outer mental barbel.
Caudal principal ray that is ventrally adjacent to caudal principal ray 9.
Caudal principal ray that is ventrally adjacent to caudal principal ray 13.
Caudal principal ray that is ventrally adjacent to caudal principal ray 16.
Actinotrichium that is part of the pectoral fin.
Pectoral fin lepidotrichium 1 is the leading or marginal ray of the fin and articulates with the scapula.  Lepidotrichium 1 is commonly segmented but unbranched.
Pectoral fin lepidotrichium that, in a linear sequence, is the seventh most anterior pectoral ray, usually branched and segmented.
Pectoral fin lepidotrichium that, in a linear sequence, is the fifth most anterior pectoral ray , usually branched and segmented.
Third lepidotrichium of pelvic fin.
Anatomical space that is the concavity containing the eye.
Portion of vessel wall that extends to form a new vessel.
Portion of organism substance that is a gelatinous extracellular matrix structure that fills the vitreous cavity of the eye.
Head mesenchyme surrounding the immature eye that  gives rise to specialized structures of the anterior segment of the eye.
The lens capsule is a modified basement membrane that completely surrounds the ocular lens.
Developing nephron with a tubular morphology that has a renal corpuscle anlage at the distal end.
Renal duct that will develop into the mesonephric distal tubule.
Region at venious pole of heart tube that initiates heart beat.
Ring of cardiac conduction tissue around the sinoatrial region of the heart tube that performs pacemaker function.
Anatomical cluster of skeletal elements that forms the roof over the brain.
Fibrous joint connecting the parietal bones.
Fibrous joint connecting the frontal bone to the parietal bone.  This joint remains patent in zebrafish throughout their lifetime.
Joint in which the articulating bones are connected by bone.
Skeletal tissue that is part of the exoskeleton and derived from an odontogenic papilla.
Fossa where the exoccipital forms the medial portion and the epioccipital forms the lateral margin.
Fibrous joint that articulates the posterior edge of the  preopercle horizontal limb with the symplectic.
Ligament that connects one rib to another.
Ligament that connects the dentary to the maxilla.
Ligament that connects the  rostral process of the maxilla  to the kinethmoid.
The ligament that connects the anteroventral tips of ceratobranchials 5 medially.
Ligament that connects the  preopercle to the retroarticular anteroventrally.
Joint that articulates the mesethmoid and vomer. Mesethmoid-vomer joint is unpaired.

Adductor that originates at the cleithrum the muscle fibers run in sheets along the endoskeletal disk extending dorsally and caudally from its base. Distally, the muscles insert onto the fin membrane.
Portion of tissue in the vagal lobe that contains GABAergic sensory interneurons.
Multi-tissue structure of the intestine comprising of the intestinal epithelium and the intestinal lamina propria mucosa.

Multi-tissue structure part of the olfactory bulb  that  is roughly spheroidal and encircled by olfactory sensory neuron axons that formed an anatomically distinct stalk  connected to the olfactory nerve.
Bilaterally-paired nerve connecting each segment of the spinal cord to the limbs and organs.
Protoglomeruli in the central zone  of the glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb.  The central zone protoglomeruli have somewhat indistinct boundaries.
Ventral region of the glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb.
Glomerulus located in the ventromedial zone of the olfactory bulb. Stains strongly with anti-calretinin.  Posteriormost glomerulus in the triplet of glomeruli strongly expressing calretinin.
Glomerulus located in the ventromedial zone of the olfactory bulb. Posterior to the triplet of  ventromedial glomeruli strongly expressing calretinin.
Glomerulus located in the lateral zone of the olfactory bulb. LG1 is surrounded by a diffuse aggregate of OSN axons.
Glomerulus located in the lateral zone of the olfactory bulb.
Glomerulus located in the lateral zone of the olfactory bulb.
Glomerulus located in the lateral zone of the olfactory bulb.
Glomerulus located in the lateral zone of the olfactory bulb. LG5 is surrounded by a diffuse aggregate of OSN axons.
Protoglomeruli in the lateral  region of the glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb.
Protoglomeruli in the medial  region of the glomerular layer of the olfactory bulb.
Cranial motor neurons found in the midbrain and hindbrain that innervates muscles that control eye and tongue.

A system of osteocytes connected through canals within the vertebra.  Osteocytes extend processes through canals within ossified bone.  The lacunocanalicular system is poorly developed in zebrafish with most  osteocytes having one or two cytoplasmic processes.

Portion of the intestinal rod that loops to left between 26-30hpf and gives rise to the intestinal bulb and liver and anterior pancreatic primordium.  The endoderm at this stage is a compact mass of cells with little to no polarization.
Polypeptide producing cell located in the islets of the pancreas.
Cells that  form an epithelial-like sheath around the vacuolated inner notochord cells. Outer cells secrete a thick extracellular perinotochordal basement membrane.
Adipose tissue deposited along the mandible.
Diploid cell produced by the fusion of sperm cell nucleus and egg cell.
Neuron that is part of the enteric nervous system.
The juncture where the  intestine empties into the cloaca.
Striated muscle of the esophogus. Permits voluntary swallowing.
Vein thats tarts posterior of the hypophysis and drains the hypophyseal capillaries.  It empties into the primary head sinus.

Axon tract originating  from the two hemispheres of the neurosecretory preoptic areas  converging into the midline and terminating at the ventral part of the hypothalamus at the presumed location of the pituitary. Analogous to the supraopticohypophyseal tract in mammals.
Surface structure that is a keratinized epidermal appendages that is a contact organ and secondary sex organ.

children.name: second tier layer of breeding tubercle

definitions.definition: The interrenal vessel (IRV) is the blood vessels supplying the interrenal gland. It is formed by sprouting from the dorsal aorta.  The development of the IRV is temporally and spatially correlated with the initiation interrenal gland formation.  After traversing the interrenal tissue, the IRV connects  to the posterior end segment of the anterior mesenteric artery where two branches of swim bladder arteries branched out.  Angiogenic sprout is visible between 34 and 48 hpf with blood flow by 3dpf.
Gelatinous substance surrounding the kinocila of the neuromast.

name: rhombencephalic efferent neurons to the lateral line

synonyms.name: rhombencephalic efferent neurons to the lateral line

definitions.definition: Efferent neuron where the cell body is located in the hindbrain reticular formation immediately adjacent to the medial longitudinal fascicle at the rostrocaudal level between the MiDl and the CaD and adjacent to the descending Mauthner axon.  RELL dendrites are large and extend bilaterally into the ventrolateral neuropil.  The ipsilateral dendrite reaches into a single area of the ventrolateral neuropil whereas the contralateral dendrite branches and extends into two different levels of the same rostrocaudal column of the ventrolateral neuropil. The axon emerges from the ventral part of the perikaryon courses a short distance rostrally to the level of the ROLE  cells and then turns laterally from the CNS accompanying the root of the posterior lateral line nerve.
Is an interconnected tubular multi-tissue structure that contains fluid that is actively transported around the heart.
Paired superfical caudal fin muscle that is located dorsally and extends from the myoseptum to the dorsal tip of the caudal fin where it attaches in the region of the second upper long fin ray.
A cell of a  hematopoietic lineage.
Lymphangiogenic sprout that  originates from the common cardinal vein and extends along the primary head sinus.

properties.value:
Although a facial lymphatic vessel has previously been described using lymphangiography in 5-week-old zebrafish (Yaniv et al., 2006), we are not sure whether
this previously described vessel is connected to, or derived from, the FL network that we have identified (ZDB-PUB-120529-43).

definitions.definition: Facial lymph vessel that sprouts from the lateral facial lymph vessel.  The path of the medial vessel runs ventromedially towards the ventral aorta.
Lymph vessel on the left of the intestine that runs parallel to the upper right intestinal lymph vessel.  There does not appear to be an associated blood vessel.
Lymph vessel that connects lymph vessels within the intestinal lymphatic network.
Ceratobranchial 5 tooth which is the posteriormost tooth in the ventral tooth row. This tooth develops from the dental epithelium  at the position of  primary tooth 5V.
Lymph vessels within the ovary.  These vessels are located in the interstitium between ovarian follicles and  appear to envelop arterioles.
Pectoral fin muscle.  Links pectoral fin and branchial movement and stabilizes the pectoral girdle.  Thought to be the teleost homologue of the cucullaris muscle group.

name: external granular layer of the cerebellar plate

synonyms.name: external granular layer of the cerebellar plate

definitions.definition: Proliferative region that forms on peripheral side of the cerebellar plate.

name: commissure of the tract of the commissure of the caudal tuberculum

synonyms.name: commissure of the tract of the commissure of the caudal tuberculum

definitions.definition: Commissure that is formed by a subset of TCPT axons that cross the midline in the diencephalon.  The TCPTc does not appear to cross with other commissures.  The initial crossing of the TCPTc occurs at approximately 36 hpf.
Epithelium that lines the seminiferous tubules.

Structure in the testis formed by cytoplasmic projections of one or two Sertoli cells that surround a single spermatogonium.  Sperm production occurs with in the cyst and the spermatogonium divides to generate approximately 1300 mature sperm.  A given Sertoli cell is in contact with only one germ cell clone.
Foramen that has the exoccipital as the anterior and dorsal rim. The occipital forms the anterior rim during early development.
Foramen in the exoccipital through which the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) passes.
Tissue that lies between the caudal artery and the caudal vein plexus where definitive hematopoiesis occurs after  48hpf and before the hematopoietic progenitors migrate to the thymus and kidney.
The initial growth point of the scale.  In zebrafish the focus is on the anterior edge of the scale.
Thread-like fibrous aggregation of secreted molecules extending from the subcommissural organ (SCO) through the ventricular system and central canal to the end of the spinal cord.
Portion of tissue that is presumed to give rise to the  entopenduncular nucleus.

inverseRoles.relatedName: ventral entopeduncular nucleus of ventral telencephalon

definitions.definition: Pouch at the end of the endolymphatic duct that helps regulates pressure on the inner ear. The endolymphatic sac is separated from the endolymphatic duct by a dynamic lamellar barrier.  The lamellar barrier is composed of long, thin lamellar sheets that form tongue-and-groove structure or interwoven broadly overlapping structures. In adults, the endolymphatic duct and sac are partially encased within the temporal bone such that the distal end of the endolymphatic sac protrudes out of the temporal bone into the cranial cavity .
Layer of melanophores that are positioned behind the argenta.  The melanophore layer absorbs unfocused light preventing it from reaching the retina.
Early-forming neural cluster located in the rostral diencephalon.  At 19 h, axons arising from the vrc grow caudally to pioneer the tract of the postoptic commissure (TPOC).

Early-forming neural cluster of the ventral midbrain.  At 16 h, axons of the vcc grow caudally to pioneer the medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF), which is part of the larger ventral longitudinal tract (VLT).  Later, neurons from this cluster project axons rostrally into the tract of the post-optic commissure (TPOC).
Surface structure that is one of the fleshy folds surrounding the opening of the mouth.
Is a mandibular muscle that attaches to Meckel's cartilage and functions during jaw closing.

In the adult bilaterally paired compact tract located lateral to the medial forebrain bundle that extends to the diencephalon. Formed from several fascicles that  originate in the precommissural telencephalon and converge rostrocaudally.  In the seven day old fish bilaterally paired bundle that runs caudally from the anterior commissure to the forebrain. In the caudal diencephalon the bundle divides into two parts. The thinner part runs more laterally and ventrally, and the thicker part was located more medially and dorsally. Both bundles run in the caudal direction toward the cranial wall of the lateral recess of  the diencephalic ventricle, where they apparently exchange some fibers. Then, they continue in the caudal  direction, surrounding the lateral recess from the ventral and dorsal side, and meet close to the caudal wall of lateral recess at the level of the commissure of the posterior tuberculum.
Posterior portion of the neural plate  that gives rise to the posterior neural keel.
Anterior portion of anterior neural plate that gives rise to the forebrain neural keel.
Portion of the posterior neural plate that gives rise to the spinal cord neural keel.
Portion of anterior neural rod that gives rise to the forebrain midbrain boundary neural tube.
Rostral portion of the neural tube.
Portion of the posterior neural tube that gives rise to the spinal cord.
Portion of neural plate that gives rise to the midbrain hindbrain boundary neural keel.
Is a mandibular muscle that attaches Meckel's cartilage to the basihyal cartilage and functions in jaw opening.
Is a ventral paired hyoid muscle that has attachment sites on the basihyal and the posterior end of the ceratohyals and functions in jaw opening.
Blood vessel within the eye.
Neurogenic field fated to develop into a dorsolateral placode.
Is a portion of tissue that is the most anterior portion of the notochord. The flexural organ secretes Reissner's fiber-related proteins, including F-spondin.
Is a three-chambered blood sinus found at the base of the maxillary barbel. Responsible, in part, for the movement of the maxillary barbel.

children.name: accessory chamber of the maxillary blood sinus
central chamber of the maxillary blood sinus
distal bulb of the maxillary blood sinus

definitions.definition: Migratory neural crest population that develops from premigratory neural crest. This group of neural crest has undergone ectomesenchymal transition and delamination.
Migratory trunk neural crest population that develops from premigratory trunk neural crest. This group of neural crest has undergone ectomesenchymal transition and delamination.
Cell that is part of the premigratory trunk neural crest population. Will undergo epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination to become part of the migratory trunk neural crest.
Vertebra that is posteriorly adjacent to vertebra 20.
Vertebra that is posteriorly adjacent to vertebra 26.
An anatomical cluster composed of the organs of the  pleuroperitoneal cavity and associated structures.
A stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system.

A cylindrical epithelial cell in the innermost layer of the enamel organ. Their functions include contribution to the development of the dentinoenamel junction by the deposition of a layer of the matrix, thus producing the foundation for the prisms (the structural units of the dental enamel), and production of the matrix for the enamel prisms and interprismatic substance. (From Jablonski's Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992).
A specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue, which typically differentiates from monocytes.

properties.value: Morphology: Highly vesicular; markers: Surface: RANK, cFMS (MCSF receptor); Secreted: cathepsin K and TRAP (tartate resistant acid phosphatase); transcription factors: PU.1, cFOS, MITF, NFkB (p52); role or process: tissue remodelling: bone resorption; lineage: hematopoietic, myeloid.

definitions.definition: A leukocyte with abundant granules in the cytoplasm.

A fully differentiated neutrophil, a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.

Pioneer neurons establish a pathway in the developing central nervous system and then undergo programmed cell death once the adult axons, which follow them, have made connections with the target site. Thus, they are a transient cell type involved in axon guidance.

A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from 'star' cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with 'end feet' which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and 'reactive astrocytes' (along with microglia) respond to injury.
Cell of the single layer of large flattened cells covering the surface of the cornea.
A cell of an exocrine gland, i.e. a gland that discharges its secretion via a duct.

A cell that stores epinephrine secretory vesicles. During times of stress, the nervous system signals the vesicles to secrete their hormonal content. Their name derives from their ability to stain a brownish color with chromic salts. Characteristically, they are located in the adrenal medulla and paraganglia of the sympathetic nervous system.
A type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of an immunoglobulin complex.
A mature sexual reproductive cell having a single set of unpaired chromosomes.
An acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces prolactin.
A connective tissue cell of an organ found in the loose connective tissue. These are most often associated with the uterine mucosa and the ovary as well as the hematopoietic system and elsewhere.
A neuron which conveys sensory information centrally from the periphery.
A cell of the B cell, T cell, or natural killer cell lineage.

A neutrophil precursor in the granulocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between a myelocyte and the band form neutrophil. The protein synthesis seen in earlier stages decreases or stops; the nucleus becomes indented and its chromatin becomes coarse and clumped; and the cytoplasm becomes pink like that of a mature granulocyte.
A specialized osteoclast associated with the absorption and removal of cementum.
A receptor in the vascular system, particularly the aorta and carotid sinus, which is sensitive to stretch of the vessel walls.

A primordial germ cell is a diploid germ cell precursors that transiently exist in the embryo before they enter into close association with the somatic cells of the gonad and become irreversibly committed as germ cells.
A stem cell that can give rise to cell types of the body other than those of the germ-line.

properties.value: Definition originally referred to GO:0048103.  Changed to GOC: CJM to match other references.

definitions.definition: An achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages, found in blood or other tissue.
A neuron that laterally connects other neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina.
A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with cone photoreceptor cells and neurons in the inner plexiform layer.
A immature or mature cell in the lineage leading to and including erythrocytes.

Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.
A B cell that is mature, having left the bone marrow. Initially, these cells are IgM-positive and IgD-positive, and they can be activated by antigen.
A gamma-delta T cell of the columnar epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract. Intraepithelial T cells often have distinct developmental pathways and activation requirements.

"Dermal tooth plates are variable structures.  During upper pharyngeal arch development in Astatotilapia elegans, dermal tooth plates are formed entirely of fused tooth pedicels (Huys-seune, 1983). However, in lower pharyngeals of the same species, teeth attach to a preexisting plate (Vandewalle et al., 1994). In other teleosts (e.g., cyprinid fifth ceratobranchials), there is no tooth plate per se, because tooth pedicels do not fuse to one another, but each fuses to the endochondral bone separately (see Gosline, 1985)."
